summary: Callback plugins now receive result.result already masked at all nesting levels; numbers matching secrets become the string $REDACTED$, colliding keys get numeric suffixes, std*_lines are rebuilt, and other data written outside Display must be passed through mask_secrets.
questions: Do callback plugins see real secret values in ansible-core 2.22?
Why did a number in my callback result become a string?
What parts of a task result are masked for callbacks?
Do I need to mask task names in my callback?

answer_card.title: Secret masking in callback plugins
answer_card.answer_md:
Before a callback receives a task result, every string value and string key in **`result.result`** is masked at any depth, including loop results. Existing callbacks keep working but no longer see registered secrets.

Other effects:
- An `int`/`float` whose text is a secret becomes the string `$REDACTED$`.
- Keys that mask to the same placeholder get suffixes like `$REDACTED$ (2)`.
- `stdout_lines`/`stderr_lines` are rebuilt from masked `stdout`/`stderr`.

Only `result.result` is masked. Task/play names, `warnings`, `deprecations`, `exception`, stats for `v2_playbook_on_stats()` and derived data are masked only via `Display()`. Anything written to files, sockets, HTTP, databases, etc. must go through `ansible.module_utils.secrets.mask_secrets()` first.
